terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo replays the same six requests against each limiter with a fake clock.

tasks.title: Fixed window
tasks.description:
Implement `createFixedWindowLimiter({ limit, windowMs, now })` in `src/fixedWindow.ts`. It returns `{ allow(key) }`.

- Time is split into windows aligned to 0: `[0, windowMs)`, `[windowMs, 2 * windowMs)` and so on.
- `allow(key)` returns `true` and counts the request when that key has made fewer than `limit` allowed requests in the current window. Otherwise it returns `false`.
- Keys are counted separately.
- `now` defaults to `Date.now`.
nextSteps: Destructure the options and give `now` a default.
Keep a `Map` from key to the window it is in and its count.
On each call work out the current window from `now()` and compare.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the first line.
hints: You never need a timer. Every decision can be made from the current time and what you stored for the key.
Which window does a time belong to? Dividing by `windowMs` and rounding down gives you a number that is the same for every time in that window.
Store `{ window, count }` per key. If the stored window is not the current one, start a new count before you compare with `limit`.

tasks.title: Sliding window
tasks.description:
Implement `createSlidingWindowLimiter({ limit, windowMs, now })` in `src/slidingWindow.ts`.

- `allow(key)` at time `T` returns `true` when that key has fewer than `limit` allowed requests at times `t` with `T - windowMs < t <= T`. The request is then recorded.
- Refused requests are not recorded and never count.
- Keys are counted separately.
nextSteps: Keep a list of allowed request times per key.
On each call drop the times that have left the window.
Compare what is left with `limit`, and record the time only when you allow.
Run the demo and compare its line with the fixed window.
hints: The fixed window lets a caller make `2 * limit` requests in a short burst across a window edge. Remembering times instead of a count fixes that.
A request at time `t` is still inside the window while `t > now - windowMs`. Mind whether the edge itself is in or out.
Filter the key's times to the recent ones, save the filtered list back, then push the current time only on the path that returns true.

tasks.title: Token bucket
tasks.description:
Implement `createTokenBucket({ capacity, refillPerSecond, now })` in `src/tokenBucket.ts`. It returns `{ take(key, cost), tokens(key) }`.

- Each key has its own bucket that starts full with `capacity` tokens.
- Tokens refill continuously at `refillPerSecond` (250 ms at 2 per second adds 0.5). A bucket never holds more than `capacity`.
- `take(key, cost = 1)` returns `true` and removes `cost` tokens when the bucket holds at least `cost`. Otherwise it returns `false` and removes nothing.
- `tokens(key)` returns the current tokens, fractions included.
nextSteps: Store `{ tokens, at }` per key, where `at` is when you last updated it.
Write one small function that brings a bucket up to date with `now()`.
Run the demo and check the third line.
hints: Like the windows, a bucket never needs a timer. You can work out how full it is from how much time has passed.
Elapsed milliseconds divided by 1000, times `refillPerSecond`, is what to add. Cap the result at `capacity`.
After adding the refill, set `at` to the current time. Otherwise the next call counts the same time again.
